title: Evaluate expressions
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.alg.evaluate.substitute: Put the number in for x. A number next to x means multiply: 3x is 3 × x. Then use the order of operations.
hints.alg.evaluate.negative: Put the negative number in with parentheses: x = −3 makes x² into (−3)² = 9, and 10 − x into 10 − (−3) = 13.
hints.alg.evaluate.two-letters: Put each number in for its own letter, then use the order of operations.
hints.alg.evaluate: Put each number in (negatives in parentheses), then do the order of operations.

misconceptionMessages.alg.eval-concatenate: 3x means 3 times x. When x = 4, 3x = 3 × 4 = 12, not 34.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eval-coefficient-squared: Only x is squared in 3x². Square x first, then multiply by 3: when x = 2, 3x² = 3 × 4 = 12.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eval-sign-dropped: Keep the negative sign: put the number in with parentheses. 10 − (−2) = 10 + 2 = 12.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eval-square-sign: A negative times a negative is positive: (−3)² = (−3) × (−3) = 9.
misconceptionMessages.alg.eval-swapped: Check which number goes with which letter, then put each one in its own place.

similarProblemIntro: Here's the worked solution. Now try one like it.

sections.title: Put in a number
sections.objective: Find the value of an expression like 3x + 2 when x = 4.
explain: Replace the letter with the number.
Then it's an order-of-operations problem: powers, then × and ÷, then + and −.
sections.key: Replace x with its number. A number next to x means multiply: 3x is 3 × x. Then follow the order of operations.

sections.title: Put in a negative number
sections.objective: Evaluate expressions when the letter is a negative number.
explain: Put the negative number in parentheses so you keep its sign.
Then use the integer rules: subtracting a negative is adding, and a negative squared is positive.
sections.key: Put a negative number in with parentheses. 10 − x with x = −2 is 10 − (−2) = 12. (−3)² = 9.

sections.title: Two letters and formulas
sections.objective: Evaluate expressions with two letters, and formulas like A = lw.
explain: Each letter gets its own number.
A formula is the same idea: A = lw means multiply the length by the width.
sections.key: Put each number in for its own letter, then follow the order of operations.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: Put each number in (negatives in parentheses), then do the order of operations.
